children: , the networking and security company, pushed Splunk AI deeper into private infrastructure with a new Nvidia-backed AI POD built for self-managed and air-gapped environments. Cisco shares were up roughly 0.1% at $110.24, based on the latest price shown in the chart, rather than the earlier $110.96 quote.

The platform is available now, pairing Cisco infrastructure with Nvidia computing and Kubernetes. Splunk's Tokenomics tool is designed to track AI spending across agents and employee coding tools, then estimate future consumption before the billing cycle closes. Cisco is also widening the commercial opportunity beyond the data center after signing a multiyear agreement with Amazon Web Services to jointly develop security products.

Cisco said it received $9.3 billion of hyperscaler AI-infrastructure orders during fiscal 2026, equal to roughly 14.7% of its $63.3 billion annual revenue. Orders are not revenue, but that comparison shows how quickly AI infrastructure is becoming material to Cisco's business. The chart adds another valuation wrinkle: at $110.2401, Cisco trades 48.05% above its $74.46 GF Value, suggesting investors are already paying a substantial premium for that AI and security growth story.

title: Cisco Gains as Splunk Starts Tracking AI's Token Bill
